title: Locate and Identify Settings Page Heading Component
description: Find the Settings page component and identify the current heading element that needs to be resized
details: Navigate to the app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx file (or app/dashboard/page.tsx if settings is part of the main dashboard). Locate the heading element that displays 'Settings' - this is likely an h1 or h2 tag with existing Tailwind CSS classes like 'text-2xl font-bold' or similar. Document the current class structure and semantic HTML tag being used to ensure proper accessibility is maintained.
test_strategy: Visual inspection of the Settings page to confirm the correct heading element is identified. Check the browser developer tools to verify the current CSS classes applied to the heading.

title: Update Heading Font Size with Responsive Design
description: Modify the Tailwind CSS classes to increase the heading font size while maintaining responsive behavior
details: Update the heading element's className to use a larger font size utility class. Change from current size (likely text-2xl) to text-3xl or text-4xl. Implement responsive design by using Tailwind's responsive prefixes (e.g., 'text-3xl md:text-4xl lg:text-5xl') to ensure the heading looks appropriate on all screen sizes. Maintain existing styling properties like font-weight and color while only modifying the font-size related classes.
test_strategy: Test the updated heading across multiple viewport sizes (mobile: 375px, tablet: 768px, desktop: 1024px+) using browser developer tools. Verify that the text doesn't wrap awkwardly or cause layout issues on any screen size.

title: Validate Visual Hierarchy and Cross-Browser Compatibility
description: Ensure the larger heading maintains proper visual hierarchy and works consistently across different browsers
details: Verify that the increased heading size creates appropriate visual hierarchy without conflicting with other page elements. Check that the heading doesn't overlap with navigation elements, buttons, or content sections. Test the page in major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) to ensure consistent rendering. Confirm that the semantic HTML structure (h1, h2, etc.) remains appropriate for accessibility and SEO purposes.
test_strategy: Perform visual regression testing by comparing before/after screenshots. Use browser testing tools or manual testing across Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Run accessibility checks using browser dev tools or axe-core to ensure heading hierarchy is maintained.
